overview_scope: These samples search for “aaaaz” in a run of “a” bytes ending in one “z”.
changes: In the timed rows, the needle is “aaaaz” and the haystack contains only “a” up to the final “z”. Nelibc verifies up to 16 candidate starts directly. With more starts and a two-to-seven-byte needle, it can search for a less common byte near the end of the needle. Four nearby false matches trigger a return to the first-byte search, with direct verification when that byte also becomes common.
